title: Medical Bills, HSAs & FSAs
description: Read the plan’s statement, then the bill, then the account that can pay it.
wolfLine: The biggest number on the letter is not always the one you owe.

itemized-bill.definition: A bill that lists every service, test, and supply with its own price, instead of one total.
itemized-bill.example: The summary said $1,240. The itemized bill showed an x-ray charged twice.

explanation-of-benefits.definition: A statement from the health plan, not a bill. It shows what was charged, what the plan allowed, what it paid, and what you may owe.
explanation-of-benefits.example: Charged $640. Allowed $400. Plan paid $320. You may owe $80.

health-savings-account.definition: A tax-favored account you can fund only with a high-deductible health plan. The money can carry over year to year and be used for qualified medical costs.
health-savings-account.example: The 2026 HSA limit is $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage, plus $1,000 if you are 55 or older.

flexible-spending-account.definition: A work account for medical costs. For 2026 the employee salary-reduction limit is $3,400. Unused money is usually lost, unless the plan allows a carryover of up to $680.
flexible-spending-account.example: You put in $3,400 for 2026 and spend $3,000. If the plan allows the maximum carryover, $400 can move forward, because $400 is under $680.

lessons.title: The Explanation of Benefits
lessons.summary: This page is the plan talking. It is not the bill.

steps.context: An [[explanation of benefits]] comes from the plan. It is not itself a bill.
steps.prompt: What is an explanation of benefits?
choices: The plan’s statement of what it allowed and what you may owe
The bill you must pay today
A receipt from the pharmacy
steps.explain: Read it before you pay. The hospital’s first number is often not your number.

lessons.title: Check the Bill
lessons.summary: Two x-rays were not what happened.

steps.context: Match the bill to the [[explanation of benefits]]. One service, one line.

doc.title: Hospital bill
doc.subtitle: Itemized
doc.note: The explanation of benefits lists one x-ray, not two.

steps.prompt: Which line does not belong?
steps.explain: The second x-ray is a double charge. The EOB listed one.

doc.title: Hospital bill
doc.subtitle: Itemized
doc.note: The explanation of benefits lists one x-ray, not two.

steps.prompt: How much is the duplicate x-ray?
steps.explain: The repeated line is $180.

steps.prompt: What should the bill add up to without that duplicate?
What do you ask the hospital for when the bill is a lump sum?
choices: An itemized bill that lists each service
A new copy of the same total
Your full medical records
steps.explain: You cannot spot a double charge on a single number.

steps.prompt: Paying a bill you have not compared to the EOB is the careful path.
steps.explain: Compare first. Then pay what you actually owe.

lessons.title: Ask for the Itemized Bill
lessons.summary: A single total hides the duplicate.

steps.context: An [[itemized bill]] lists every service with its own price. A summary bill shows one total.
steps.prompt: An itemized bill shows:
choices: Each service and its price
Only the total and the due date
What your plan paid, and nothing else
steps.explain: The lines are how you find the mistake.

steps.prompt: A one-line total is enough to check for a double charge.
steps.explain: The double hides inside the total.

steps.prompt: The itemized lines are $220, $80, and $140. What is the total?
A line says “misc.” and costs $600. What do you do?
choices: Ask what the service was
Pay it. Misc. lines are standard
Dispute the whole bill
steps.explain: A vague line is a question, not a verdict.

steps.prompt: Compare each line to the ___.
choices: explanation of benefits
premium
deductible
steps.explain: The plan already said what it allowed.

lessons.title: Negotiating and Payment Plans
lessons.summary: The first number is an offer, not always the end.

steps.context: Hospitals often have a prompt-pay discount or a monthly plan. Ask before you put it on a credit card.
steps.prompt: The bill is $3,200. The hospital offers 25% off if you pay within 30 days. How much is the discount?
How much do you pay if you take that 25% off?
A payment plan is $200 a month for 16 months. What is the total?
Which is usually worse than a hospital payment plan?
choices: A credit card at a high interest rate
Asking for an itemized bill
Reading the EOB
steps.explain: The card keeps charging after the hospital would have stopped.

steps.prompt: You have to accept the first total on the letter.
steps.explain: Ask. A discount or a plan is a normal conversation.

lessons.title: Hospital Financial Assistance
lessons.summary: Nonprofit hospitals have a program. You have to ask.

steps.title: Aid is a form, not a secret
steps.body:
Many hospitals, especially nonprofit ones, have financial assistance, sometimes called charity care. It can reduce or erase a bill if your income qualifies.

The form is the door. The program does not knock.

steps.prompt: What is hospital financial assistance?
choices: A program that can lower a bill based on your income
A hospital loan at a lower rate
A discount only for people with no insurance
steps.explain: It is aid, not a new debt.

steps.prompt: You should wait until the bill is in collections before you ask about assistance.
steps.explain: Ask while the bill is still at the hospital. Collections is a harder room.

steps.prompt: What do you ask the billing office?
choices: For the financial assistance application and the income rules
For a lower interest rate on the bill
For a new copy of the bill
steps.explain: The rules are written. Get the form.

steps.prompt: Financial assistance is based on whether your ___ qualifies.
choices: income
credit score
insurance plan
steps.explain: Bring the proof they ask for.

lessons.title: HSA or FSA
lessons.summary: One can travel with you. The other is use it, mostly, this year.

steps.context: An [[HSA|health-savings-account]] is paired with a high-deductible plan. For 2026 the limit is $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family, plus $1,000 at age 55 or older. An [[FSA|flexible-spending-account]] has a 2026 employee limit of $3,400. If the employer allows a carryover, the 2026 maximum is $680. Those figures are from the IRS for 2026.
steps.prompt: Which account is this?
items: You need a high-deductible health plan to contribute
The money can stay year after year
It is offered through work and unused money is usually lost
A 2026 carryover, if the plan allows one, is capped at $680
steps.explain: The HSA is the one that stays. The FSA is the work account with a clock.

steps.prompt: The 2026 self-only HSA limit is $4,400. You contribute $200 a month. How much is that in a year?
How much of the $4,400 limit is left?
You are 55. Add the $1,000 catch-up to the $4,400 self-only limit. What is the total you can put in for 2026?
An FSA and an HSA have the same rule about leftover money.
steps.explain: HSA money stays. FSA money is usually lost, except a carryover the plan chose to allow.

lessons.title: Why an HSA Is Favored
lessons.summary: The tax break is the point. The receipt is the proof.

steps.context: Money in an [[HSA|health-savings-account]] can go in tax-favored, and qualified medical withdrawals come out tax-free. Keep the receipts.
steps.prompt: A qualified medical expense paid from an HSA is:
choices: Generally free of income tax
Taxed as income, like a paycheck
Tax-free only if you are over 65
steps.explain: That is the favor. Sunglasses you do not need are not a qualified expense.

steps.prompt: You contribute $2,400. In a simple example your income-tax rate is 20%. How much income tax do you not pay on that contribution this year?
steps.explain: $2,400 × 0.20 = $480. Real taxes depend on your return. This is the shape of the break.

steps.prompt: You can spend HSA money on anything, tax-free, the week you deposit it.
steps.explain: A non-medical withdrawal can be taxed, and it can be penalized if you are under 65.

steps.prompt: Why keep receipts?
choices: They show the withdrawal was for a qualified medical cost
The account won’t pay without one at the register
You must mail every receipt to the IRS each year
steps.explain: The favor depends on the expense being qualified.

steps.prompt: The 2026 family HSA limit is $8,750. The self-only limit is $4,400. How much higher is the family limit?

lessons.title: Jordan’s Surprise Bill
lessons.summary: The letter shouted. The EOB whispered the real number.

story.title: The bill that was not his
story.body:
Jordan leaves the ER with a sore ankle and, two weeks later, a letter asking for **$3,200**. The [[explanation of benefits]] arrives the next day. It says the plan allowed less, paid its share, and Jordan may owe **$640**.

He has an [[HSA|health-savings-account]] with **$700** in it. He has not asked the hospital for an itemized bill yet.

steps.prompt: How much does the EOB say Jordan may owe?
steps.explain: The EOB says $640.

steps.prompt: How much of the $3,200 letter is not his, according to that EOB?
What should he do before paying the $3,200?
choices: Call billing, ask for an itemized bill, and check it against the EOB
Put $3,200 on a credit card tonight
Pay the $3,200 now and ask for a refund later
steps.explain: The letter may have gone out before the plan paid. Match it to the EOB first.

steps.prompt: His HSA has $700. After a qualified $640 payment, how much is left in the account?
Once the bill matches the EOB, Jordan can pay the $640 from his HSA.
steps.explain: An ER visit is a qualified medical cost.

choices: A double charge to dispute
Proof you had it twice
A normal follow-up fee
steps.explain: One test, one line.

steps.explain: FSA money is usually lost. A 2026 carryover, if allowed, stops at $680.
